# Tips from past games

Written 2026-10-11 10:01 by opus-5.5 with `uv run tips.py build`, from the 262 active entries of tips_notebook.json (50 games). Players never see this preamble; they see every section below. Earlier sheets are in history/.

## Everyone
- Ballots are secret, so keep a notepad of every nomination and trial: each player's stated vote, the announced totals and your own. Vote as you said you would and explain any switch first; a mismatch with the totals is a lead, never a hang on its own. (seen in 30 games)
- Totals can be manipulated. A trial total above the voter count means a Ballot Stuffer, and a Fixer silently flips one player's trial votes. Yes/No nomination counts can't be altered, so they are the cleanest liar check. (seen in 2 games)
- A visit shows a destination, not an action. But a corroborated Lookout or Tracker naming X as the only unexplained visitor to a Katana victim is near-proof; don't let 'a visit isn't an attack' acquit X. (seen in 32 games)
- Before voting Guilty, name one concrete mechanical fit: an unexplained Evil read on a Vanilla claim, a broken visit claim, or a group result where elimination leaves one name. A role-block fully explains a missing result, so that is never a contradiction. (seen in 36 games)
- Each night write your planned target in your will, and post results publicly by day. The result of the night you die never reaches your will. (seen in 29 games)
- Answer a direct question about your night action in one plain sentence the first time it is asked; days of evasion become a case of their own. (seen in 9 games)
- Tokens die with you. Spend one-shot tokens on the first Day or night they can change a vote or remove a threat, and spend a puppet or doubled ballot at least a night before a likely death. (seen in 4 games)

## Village
- Post your role, target and exact result in your first speech after getting it, and counterclaim any copier at once with your full log. Results held back look retrofitted. (seen in 18 games)
- Never announce tonight's target, in public or by PM. A Wiretap may read every PM, and a named target tells blockers and the Katana where to go. (seen in 24 games)
- On Day 2, power roles with no result should not hint at their role or lead loudly. The most organized voice is the usual Night 2 kill. (seen in 24 games)
- Once someone is shown Yakuza mechanically, look at who defended them or pushed to delay their hang. Treat PM links as leads only, since Jesters and Executioners leave trails on purpose. (seen in 30 games)
- Before any hang, ask whether the nominee wins by being hanged. If you must hang a likely Jester, use a bare Guilty majority and keep confirmed power roles on Innocent. (seen in 16 games)
- Hunt Neutral killers deliberately. Read every cause of death, list unwatched Vanilla or unclaimed players and survivors with no protector, and hang the best suspect before the final two, when you can no longer hang them. (seen in 2 games)
- Surviving an attack proves nothing, since Arsonists and Serial Killers have Standard Defense. Ask the survivor at once who protected them. (seen in 17 games)

## Yakuza
- Don't defend a doomed teammate. If your team's votes can't stop the hang, vote Guilty with the town, because hidden Innocent votes show in the totals. (seen in 38 games)
- Send no daytime PMs about team plans, and none to teammates on Day 2; plan in night chat. (seen in 34 games)
- Fake-claim a Village role whose tokens and real visits match yours. Never claim or name a Yakuza-only role, and never switch claims once cornered. (seen in 19 games)
- Every member must submit the agreed Katana holder and target every night; one missing vote can cancel the kill. (seen in 20 games)
- Never flatly deny a visit that an FT count, map group or Lookout could expose. Agree a cover in night chat, and move the Katana off any holder a watcher has named. (seen in 22 games)
- After a failed Katana attack, kill or block the likely protector instead of retrying blindly. Prioritize running counts (Fortune Teller, Census Taker) and Party Animals with block logs. (seen in 21 games)
- Use Clerk rigs, puppets and cleans early, but never rig a Day when a teammate is the likely nominee. (seen in 20 games)

## Neutral
- If innate Defense saves you, deny being attacked. If you must explain it, pick one claim at once and never switch. (seen in 6 games)

## Sheriff
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil, so say so whenever you post a Not Evil result. A lone last Yakuza reads Not Evil every night. (seen in 19 games)

## Coroner
- Examine bodies that settle live questions: one side of a duplicate claim, or a hanged suspect. Post the night, target and role in one message the next Day, and skip cleaned bodies. (seen in 3 games)

## Medic
- Use free Standard protection on likely Katana targets, vary your pattern, and never announce targets. Spend a token on self-protection within a night or two of claiming, and never claim you 'saw' a save. (seen in 24 games)

## Vigilante
- Set a trigger by Day 2-3 and fire a Basic shot on a real lead rather than dying with all tokens. A Basic shot that fails without a credible Medic points to innate Defense, so post it. (seen in 11 games)

## Smuggler
- A swap moves only actions aimed at the two swapped players. Aim the Katana at a decoy and swap the decoy with the protected real target, or swap yourself with a Villager to dodge a check. Plan it in night chat rather than vetoing it. (seen in 2 games)

## Arsonist
- Ignite once 3 living players are doused, or 2 if you are being questioned. Have a claim ready that explains your douse visits. (seen in 12 games)

rules:
=== PART 1: THE GAME ===

R1 (Overview and winning)
You are playing a Mafia-style game with around 10 players (depending on setup), each in a faction. An omniscient
moderator runs the game. The game alternates Night and Day phases, starting with Night 1: there is no Day 1, so
the first Day is Day 2 (players write their first will before Night 1).
- For most roles, you win iff your faction wins. A faction typically wins iff it has players alive at the end.
- The game ends as soon as all living players, ignoring roles that never block wins, belong to one faction. This is
  checked after every death; deaths that happen together at night are checked together.
- Some Neutral roles never block another faction's win (their role says so); their own wins don't depend on how
  the game ends.

R2 (Factions)
- Village (Good): the largest faction, but with weaker roles and less information.
- Yakuza (Evil): fewer players, stronger roles; they know each other and share a night chat.
- Neutral: each Neutral player is their own one-person faction, even if two players have the same Neutral role.
The list of roles in the game is not public. A role may appear more than once in a game, except these unique
roles, which appear at most once: Smuggler, Vulture.

R15 (Alignments)
Every player has one of three alignments: Good (Village), Evil (Yakuza) or Neutral. Some roles and effects change
how a player's alignment appears; see R19.

R18 (Terms)
- Living players: players who haven't died or left. Every count in these rules ("majority", "random player")
  means living players unless it says otherwise.
- Majority: strictly more than half; exactly half is not a majority.
- Action: anything a role does at night by choice or by its rules (investigating, shooting, blocking, ...).
- Visit: an action on another player counts as A visiting B, unless it is an Astral Visit (R6).
- Astral Visit: an action that is not a visit. Abilities that react to visits (Tracker, Lookout, Trapper,
  Fortune Teller) never see or react to it.
- Alignment check: a result that reports alignment (Sheriff, Seer). See R19 for what they see.
- Exact-role check: a result that reports or tests an exact role (Oracle, Diviner, Ritualist, Mortician, Coroner,
  Talent Agent, a Vigilante's kill).
- Token: a limited-use resource a role starts with. Spent tokens are gone; a role-blocked action spends none.

R11 (The circle)
Players sit in a circle. The dead (and players who leave) are removed from it.

=== PART 2: THE DAY ===

R4 (Day phase, chat, nominations and trials)
Chat:
- There is a public chat and private chats between exactly two players.
- Private messages are not secret: whenever A sends B a private message, everyone sees that A sent B a private
  message, but only A and B see its contents.
Nominations:
- Any player may publicly nominate someone, including themself. All chat stops at once.
- Everyone votes Yes/No at the same time; nobody sees another vote before casting their own. The nominator votes
  Yes by default. There are no abstentions: a player who doesn't vote counts as voting No. Votes are secret: once
  all votes are in, only the number of Yes votes is announced (the nominator is named), never who voted which way.
  Each voter is privately reminded of their own vote.
- If a majority of all votes counted are Yes, the nominee goes on trial.
Trials:
- The nominee says the first public message and may defend themself; others may chat publicly and privately.
  After everyone else has had a turn, the nominee gets one last public message before the vote.
- Then everyone votes Guilty/Innocent at the same time (no abstentions: a player who doesn't vote counts as voting
  Innocent). Votes are secret: only the Guilty and Innocent totals are announced, never who voted which way. Each
  voter is privately reminded of their own vote.
- If a majority of all votes counted are Guilty, the nominee is Executed by Hanging, a Divine Attack, and the Day
  ends immediately.
- If three nominations pass (failed ones don't count) and all three trials end Innocent, the Day ends.
- Some roles can change how votes are counted. If an announced vote total doesn't match the number of voters,
  a role manipulated the count on purpose; it is not an error. One use of such a role can change every trial
  that Day, so the number of changed totals doesn't show how many times a role was used.
Voting Yes or Guilty on yourself is allowed.

R16 (Day length)
Day chat goes around the circle in turns. Each Day the program picks a random living player to speak first;
turns then go around the circle from them in the same order every round. Besides the endings in R4, the Day ends when a full round passes in
which nobody sends a public message or nominates, except that anyone sent a private message during that round
first gets one last turn. The Day also ends after at most 8 rounds.

R22 (Speaking budget)
Day messages and nominations cost speaking budget. Each player earns budget every round of a Day, up to a cap,
and part of what they have left carries into the next Day. A message's price grows with its length and, after
the first rounds of a Day, with the round; private messages cost less than public ones. A nomination costs
budget too. On a trial turn prices are lower and each speaker also gets a trial-only budget, spent first and lost
when the turn ends; the accused's first defense message is free up to a set length. The program sets the
numbers for each game and tells every player at the start.

R23 (Swaps)
Some roles can swap two players for a night. Every action that night aimed at one of them (including the Katana's
attack and automatic actions such as the Ex-Con's visit or the Seer's pair) lands on the other instead, as if its
user had chosen that player. Only the swap itself is not moved (the swapping player's Katana vote is). Results name the player the action's
user chose, so a swapped action's result doesn't show the swap: a Sheriff who checked A learns B's alignment as
A's. A result that lists several players (e.g. a group around the target) is built around B, but A and B trade
places in the list, each named where the other would be; the roles, alignments and counts in it are still the real
players', so the rest of the group can still hint at the swap. A Lookout who watched A watches B instead, and a Tracker sees the player its target's action landed on.

R13 (Last wills)
Players may write and update a last will before Night 1, at the beginning of each Day (except those who died the
night before) and during any of their own Day turns. When a player dies, their last will is shared publicly at once.

=== PART 3: THE NIGHT ===

R5 (Night phase)
Chat is off for most players; some (usually a faction, like the Yakuza) have a private night chat. The moderator
wakes players one by one, or faction by faction, to act. When the Night ends, the moderator works out every
effect. By default, effects are announced publicly at the start of the next Day; some are not announced.

R7 (Optional actions)
Every ability is optional ("may") unless its role says "must": any player may choose not to act at Night, not to
use a Day ability, and not to spend a token. Effects a role has automatically, with no choice (e.g. the
Ex-Con's nightly visit), aren't optional, but a role-block still stops them (R9).

R6 (Visits)
- When A performs an action on B, A visits B, unless the action is an Astral Visit.
- A role that targets a player may target itself unless its text says otherwise (e.g. "other than yourself").
- A player whose role can target others but who targets themself shows as visiting themself.
- A player whose action can only affect themself does not show as visiting anyone.
- An action that targets no player (e.g. the Clerk's rig) is not a visit.
- A player who visits the same target with several actions in one night is one visitor to that target: anything
  that lists, counts or reacts to visitors (a watch, a Veteran's alert, a trap) treats them once.

R9 (Role-blocks)
A role-blocked player's actions that night have no effect, exactly as if they had chosen not to act: no visit,
no tokens spent. It lasts only that one night (not the next Day or later nights). Role-blocked players are told
they were role-blocked. Any player can be role-blocked unless their role says otherwise; blocking a player who
has no night action, or who chose not to act, has no other effect, but they are still told. A role-blocker learns
only whether the block failed because its target can't be role-blocked.

R10 (Simultaneous night resolution)
All night actions happen at the same time. Think of it as two steps: first everyone attempts their actions,
then all results happen together. So investigations that give their result at the end of the night (e.g. the
Seer's random pair) draw from and report on everyone alive when the night began, including players who die that
night.

R21 (Effects that outlast their user)
An effect set up at night for the following Day (e.g. a Clerk's rig, a Prosecutor's prosecution) still happens if
its user dies that night, unless it needs its user to act during that Day (e.g. a Puppeteer writing the puppet's
messages, a Ballot Stuffer's doubled vote); those lapse. Any token spent on it is gone either way (R18).

R20 (Night resolution checklist): a summary of the rules above, in the order the moderator applies them.
1. Remove actions of role-blocked players (R9), automatic ones included (the Ex-Con's visit, the Seer's pair).
   Party Animal, Pharmacist, Smuggler and Veteran can't be role-blocked. Swaps (R23) apply before anything else.
2. Work out who visits whom (R6), including the Katana holder's visit (R8) and the Ex-Con's random visit.
3. Attacks: each kills iff its level beats the target's Defense (R3). Defenses don't stack; the highest counts.
   Traps hit non-Village visitors (Trapper).
4. Results for investigators, using the visits and appearances (R19).
5. Notifications: attackers learn whether they succeeded, attacked players learn the attacking role (R3, with the
   Katana exception in R8), protectors learn nothing (R17), role-blocked players are told (R9), Yakuza learn each
   other's actions (R8).
6. Deaths are revealed at the start of the Day (R12); the win check runs on all of the night's deaths together (R1).

=== PART 4: ATTACKS, DEATH AND INFORMATION ===

R3 (Attack and Defense)
- Levels, lowest to highest: None, Basic, Standard, Strong, Divine. Players have Defense None by default.
- An Attack kills iff its level is strictly higher than the target's Defense.
- Defenses don't stack: a player with several sources of Defense has the highest of them.
- By default the attacker learns whether the Attack succeeded (not the target's Defense), and the target learns
  the role that attacked them (not the attacker's name or Attack level). The Katana is an exception (R8).

R17 (Protection feedback)
Protectors (e.g. the Medic) are never told whether their protection stopped an attack, and a protected player is
never told who protected them. A player who is attacked is still told as in R3.

R12 (Death reveals)
When someone dies, their cause of death (e.g. Katana, Vigilante, Execution by Hanging) and last will are revealed
publicly; their role and alignment are not. If several attacks were each fatal, every fatal cause is revealed;
attacks the player survived aren't. The dead leave the circle and can't take part in the game any more. A player
whose win ends their part in the game (a hanged Jester, an Executioner who leaves) is the exception: the
announcement of their win names their role.

R14 (Stall rule)
If a Day begins and nobody has died in the three previous Nights and three previous Days, everyone loses. Deaths
from last Night count even though they're announced today. Every death counts; leaving (like the Executioner's)
doesn't.

R19 (What investigations see)
Alignment checks (Sheriff: Evil / Not Evil; Seer: compares Good / Neutral / Evil) see a player's true alignment,
except:
- Yakuza holding the Katana at the end of the night: Good (Sheriff: Not Evil), even if they died that night.
- Player framed by the Fabricator that night: Evil.
- Ex-Con: Evil.
- Sheriff on Neutrals: Jester and Executioner read Evil; Serial Killer and Arsonist read Not Evil. (Seers see
  every Neutral as Neutral.)
The Census Taker's count is not an alignment check: it always sees true alignment, so none of the exceptions
above apply to it.
Exact-role checks see the true role. The Roleplayer is seen as "Roleplayer".
Token counts (Accountant) see the true total at the end of the night. The Roleplayer is seen as having 0 tokens,
even though they believe they have their fake role's tokens.
Visit-based results (Tracker, Lookout, Fortune Teller, Cartographer, Scout) are never changed by any of these.

=== PART 5: THE YAKUZA ===

R8 (Yakuza and the Katana)
- One random Yakuza starts with the Katana. The Yakuza share a private chat at night.
- Each night the Yakuza vote, at the same time, on who holds the Katana that night (and the next Day) and whom it
  attacks, if anyone. Both choices need a majority of living Yakuza; with two Yakuza alive, both must agree.
  Without a majority on a target, no attack happens; without a majority on a holder, the Katana doesn't move.
  A majority may move the Katana without attacking.
- The Katana attack is Standard and is dealt by whoever holds it at the end of the night. It is an action and a
  visit by that player (the new holder, if it moved that night): role-blocking them stops it, and Trackers see
  them visit the target. Moving or passing the Katana isn't an action: a role-block doesn't stop it (a blocked
  new holder still gets the Katana, but their attack fails), and it isn't a visit.
- The holder may also use their own role's night action.
- The holder appears Good to alignment checks that night (R19).
- The attacked player only learns they were attacked with the Katana, not the Yakuza role.
- At the end of the night, each Yakuza learns what actions the other Yakuza chose, but not their results
  (e.g. whether the Pharmacist's block worked) or whether a teammate was role-blocked.
- Role-blocked Yakuza still vote on the Katana's holder and target; the votes aren't actions.
- If the holder dies, the Katana passes to a random living Yakuza, if any; a holder who dies at night passes it on
  after that night's results. The living Yakuza are told who holds it now (and so learn that the holder died).

=== PART 6: ROLES ===

Every role lists the same fields. Defaults, unless a role says otherwise: Defense None, no tokens, appears as its
true alignment (R19), night action is a visit.

--- Village (Good) ---

Townsfolk (most villagers, helpful to the Village)

Vanilla Villager
  Night: none.

Investigative

Sheriff
  Night: may investigate one player. Learn Evil or Not Evil (alignment check, R19).

Tracker
  Night: may track one player. Learn whom they visited.

Lookout
  Night: may watch one player. Learn who visited them, not counting your own visit.

Seer
  Tokens: 1 seer token.
  Night: at the end of every night, you are told two random players other than yourself who were alive when the
  night began (players who die that night count, R10), and whether their alignments (Good/Neutral/Evil) are the
  same (alignment check, R19). Instead, you may spend a token to choose the
  two living players yourself (not including yourself). A chosen pair is a visit to both players; the random
  pair isn't a visit. A role-block stops both.

Fortune Teller
  Night: at the end of every night, you learn two numbers about that night, each labeled: how many players were
  visited (a player visited several times counts once), and how many players visited anyone (a player who visited
  several players counts once). This needs no action. Self-visits (R6) count in both numbers.
  Example: A holds the Katana, attacks B and also uses their own role's action on C, D visits B, and E protects
  themself. Visited: B, C and E, so 3. Visitors: A, D and E, so 3. Equal numbers don't mean nobody was visited
  twice.

Oracle
  Night: may guess one player's exact role (Astral Visit). At the end of the night, learn whether you were right.

Eavesdropper
  Night: may eavesdrop on one player. Only during the following Day (not the Night you eavesdrop), you read the contents of every private
  message they send or receive, as it is sent. Puppeted messages reach you as the puppet's (you aren't told about
  the puppeting). They aren't told.

Archivist
  Tokens: 1 archive token.
  Night: may spend the token to consult the archive. At the end of the night, let N be the number of players other
  than you who were alive when the night began (players who died that night count): you are shown N roles, in
  random order and without names, of which floor(0.5 * N) are real and the rest are fake. The real ones are the
  roles of floor(0.5 * N) of those players, chosen at random; a role appears as many times as it was drawn, so
  two drawn Vanilla Villagers show twice. This is an exact-role check (R19).
  Each fake is drawn at random from all the roles in these rules, including roles that are in the game, except
  that the result never shows a unique role (R2) twice.

Surveyor
  Tokens: 3 survey tokens.
  Night: may spend a token to survey one player other than yourself. The group is that player plus their nearest
  neighbor on each side in the circle (R11) among the players alive at the start of the night, skipping yourself
  and never counting anyone twice (so with only one or two other players alive, the group is smaller). You are
  told who was in the group and the exact role of one of them chosen at random, but not whose it is. Players who
  die that night can still be chosen. This is an exact-role check (R19).

Census Taker
  Night: may take a census around one player other than yourself (a visit to that player only).
  The program adds two other players drawn at random from everyone alive at the start of the night except you
  (players who die that night can be drawn; if fewer than two others are left, the group is smaller). It also
  draws at random whether to count Good or Evil players. You are told who was in the group, which alignment was
  counted, and how many of the group are of it. It counts true alignment and is not an alignment check (R19):
  the Katana holder, framed players and the Ex-Con count as what they really are, and
  Outsiders (e.g. the Roleplayer and the Ex-Con) count as Good. Neutral players are never
  counted, as either Good or Evil.

Coroner
  Tokens: 3 coroner tokens.
  Night: may spend a token to examine one player who died before the night began (not one who left the game, and not
  one who dies tonight). You learn their role, unless a Mortician cleaned them: then you learn only that. This is an
  Astral Visit (R6) and an exact-role check (R19).

Chronicler
  Tokens: 2 chronicler tokens.
  Night: may spend a token to mark one player other than yourself. This is a visit. The marked player isn't told.
  The mark lasts for the rest of the game, even after you die. If a marked player dies, at any time and of any
  cause, the announcement of their death also reveals their true role to everyone (an exact-role check, R19), and
  says they had been marked by a Chronicler (not by whom). A Mortician's clean beats the mark: a marked player who
  is cleaned has their role and will hidden, and the announcement says they had been marked but the clean hid their
  role. You can't mark a player you already marked. Marking a player another Chronicler already marked spends your
  token but adds nothing.

Auditor
  Night: may audit one player other than yourself. You learn every vote they cast during the Day just before this
  Night, in order: Yes or No on each nomination and Guilty or Innocent in each trial. If they cast none, you learn
  that. A doubled vote (Ballot Stuffer) shows as a single Guilty or Innocent.

Juror
  Night: may name two different players other than yourself (dead players allowed; Astral Visit). You learn how many
  times they voted the same way, over every Day so far, counted separately for trial votes (Guilty/Innocent) and
  nomination votes (Yes/No), e.g. "the same way in 3 of 4 trial votes and 5 of 9 nomination votes". Only votes
  both of them cast count, and not votes on the nomination or trial of either of them. A doubled vote (Ballot
  Stuffer) counts once. You learn only the totals, not which votes they agreed on.

Bloodhound
  Tokens: 2 scent tokens.
  Night: at the end of every night, code draws three random players other than you from those alive at the start of
  the night, and you learn their names and how many Attacks (R3) they have made in total this game, tonight's
  included, whether or not the Attacks killed anyone. Each player's Katana attacks, shots, alert or trap hits and
  so on all count; a role-blocked attack never happened, so it doesn't. This needs no action and a role-block
  doesn't stop it.
  Night: may also spend a token to track one player other than yourself: they take one of the three places that
  night and code draws the other two. A role-block stops the tracking (R9) but not the result.

Scrutineer
  Night: may scrutinize one player other than yourself who voted in the Day's trials (Astral Visit). Code adds two
  random other players who voted in those trials (never you), and you learn the three names and, for each trial of
  the Day just before this Night, how many of the three voted Guilty, e.g. "2 in the trial of Erin; 0 in the trial
  of Frank". You don't learn which of them voted which way. A doubled vote (Ballot Stuffer) counts once. If there
  was no trial that Day, you learn that.

Profiler
  Tokens: 3 profile tokens.
  Night: may spend a token to profile one player other than yourself. You learn three different roles, exactly one
  of which is that player's true role. Of the other two, one is drawn at random from the roles of the other players
  alive at the start of the night (including players who die that night, but not yourself), and the other from the
  roles that no player in the game has. At least one of the three is a Good role and at least one is not Good (Evil
  or Neutral), so a result never settles the player's alignment on its own; which of the two supplies the missing
  side is random. When no role fits a draw, that one is drawn from all roles in these rules instead. The three are
  different and listed in alphabetical order. This is an exact-role check (R19).

Cartographer
  Tokens: 2 map tokens.
  Night: at the end of every night, you learn the sizes of that night's visit groups. Link two players whenever one
  visited the other that night (R6). Direction is ignored: A visiting B links them exactly as B visiting A
  would. A group is a set of players linked to each other, directly or through other players. Every player alive at
  the start of the night (including players who die that night) is in exactly one group, so a player who visited no
  one and was visited by no one is a group of 1, and a self-visit links no one. You learn only the sizes, largest
  first (e.g. "4, 2, 1, 1, 1"). This needs no action and a role-block doesn't stop it.
  Night: may also spend a token to map one player (Astral Visit; yourself allowed): at the end of the night you also
  learn the names of everyone in that player's group. A role-block stops the map (R9) but not the sizes.
  Your own actions never visit anyone, so they never link you to anyone.

Scout
  Night: at the end of every night, you learn the names of three players (you may be one of them) who were each in a
  different visit group that night. Groups are as for the Cartographer (visit direction is ignored). The names are
  drawn like this: a random player, then a random player outside the groups already drawn from, and so on, so a big
  group is more likely to come up than a small one. If there were fewer than three groups, you learn one name per
  group and how many groups there were. This needs no action and a role-block doesn't stop it. You never visit
  anyone.

Insomniac
  Tokens: 2 insomniac tokens.
  Night: may spend a token to stay awake. At the end of the night, you learn the roles of up to 3 players who visited
  someone that night (R6; a visit to themselves counts), but not who they are: if more than 3 players visited, 3 of
  them are drawn at random. The roles are listed in alphabetical order, and a role shows twice if two of those
  players have it. If fewer than 3 players visited, you learn all of their roles, and if nobody visited, you learn
  that. Players who visited and then died that night count. Only visits count: an action that isn't a visit (e.g.
  an Astral Visit or a Veteran's alert) doesn't. Staying awake is not a visit. This is an exact-role check (R19).

Accountant
  Night: may audit one player. Learn how many tokens they have in total at the end of the night, after any they
  spent that night and any a Magpie stole (token count, R19). You learn only the total, not what kind of tokens
  they are.

  Tokens: 1 attack token. Never blocks wins (R1).

Resolve all actions simultaneously per the rules, following the R20 checklist (R10; visits R6, role-blocks R9, attack vs defense R3, investigation results R19, e.g. the Katana holder and Fabricator frames). Use apply_changes for deaths and token/status changes, tell() for each private result, and end_phase when done. Deaths you apply are announced publicly at dawn automatically, including the kill's cause, so make the cause just the source as the rules allow it to be known (e.g. 'Katana', 'Vigilante', 'Serial Killer', 'Trap'). For each kill also set `by` to the player whose action killed them (the trap's owner for a trap) and katana=true for the Katana attack; these are recorded for analysis, never shown. Don't tell() deaths to all. Every attacked player, including those who died, gets their attack notice (R20 step 5), saying whether they died; moderators have skipped it, or left out the death, for players who died. Tell each role-blocked player that they were role-blocked, even one with no night action or who chose not to act (R9); a role-blocker learns only whether the block failed because its target can't be role-blocked (R9). Write private results in the present, about tonight ('You were role-blocked tonight'), never 'last night': they are delivered at the end of this night. Every player who used an ability gets a private result line, even when nothing else happened (e.g. 'You went on alert. 1 alert token left.'), stating any tokens they have left, except where a role note below says otherwise (e.g. code tells them, so don't tell() them a second result). Tell all Yakuza which actions each Yakuza chose but not the results, nor whether a teammate was role-blocked (R8); role-blocked Yakuza's Katana votes still count. only the attacker learns whether the Katana attack succeeded. Update token counts for any tokens spent. Before end_phase, call record_visits once with every visit that happened tonight (R6, R20 steps 1-2), as [visitor, target] pairs, a self-visit as [X, X] (an empty list if there were none). Easy to miss: the Katana holder visits the Katana target (R8) besides any visit from their own role's action; automatic visits (the Ex-Con's); a Seer's chosen pair is a visit to both players. Leave out the actions of role-blocked players, Astral Visits and actions that target no player. The submitted actions above already show any swap (R23), so record each visit to the player it landed on.

Also handle these roles' effects, using random_choice for anything random:
- A Ballot Stuffer who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the stuff_ballot op, which spends the token; code doubles their trial votes tomorrow.
- A Bounty Hunter's attack is a Strong Attack that spends its attack token: pass by=<the Bounty Hunter> on the kill op, since code credits its bounties from the killers. Code tells it which bounties it claimed or lost and handles its win or loss; don't tell() it about bounties.
- A Fixer who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the fix op, which spends the token; code counts the player's trial votes tomorrow as the opposite; nobody is told. It is a visit to the target only.
- A Juror who acted (and wasn't role-blocked) and named two different players other than themselves (target and second_target; dead players allowed): use the jury op with those two players; code tells the Juror the result. Don't tell() the Juror anything about it. It is an Astral Visit, so it visits no one.
- Ritualist who spent tokens (and wasn't role-blocked): compare the guessed role with the target's exact role (a Roleplayer is a Roleplayer). Right: deal the Attack (1 token Standard, 2 Divine). Wrong: no Attack; announce it with tell(['all'], '<name> is a Ritualist.') tonight, which is read out at the start of the next Day, even if the Ritualist dies tonight. Astral Visit.
- A Scrutineer who acted (and wasn't role-blocked): use the scrutinize op; code draws two others and tells them how many of the three voted Guilty in each of the Day's trials. Don't tell() the Scrutineer anything about it. It is an Astral Visit, so it visits no one.
- Smuggler: code has already carried out each swap below (spent the token, redirected every other action in the JSON and told the Smuggler and both swapped players), so resolve the actions as given and tell none of them about the swap. Actions it moved keep the player's own choice in `chosen_target` / `chosen_second_target`: word every private result with the player the action's user chose, never the one it landed on, and in a list of players trade the swapped pair's names (each where the other would be), so the swap stays hidden (rules R23). Give ops the player an action landed on: code words its own results this way. The Smuggler visits both swapped players (R6); it can't be role-blocked.

Resolve all actions simultaneously per the rules, following the R20 checklist (R10; visits R6, role-blocks R9, attack vs defense R3, investigation results R19, e.g. the Katana holder and Fabricator frames). Use apply_changes for deaths and token/status changes, tell() for each private result, and end_phase when done. Deaths you apply are announced publicly at dawn automatically, including the kill's cause, so make the cause just the source as the rules allow it to be known (e.g. 'Katana', 'Vigilante', 'Serial Killer', 'Trap'). For each kill also set `by` to the player whose action killed them (the trap's owner for a trap) and katana=true for the Katana attack; these are recorded for analysis, never shown. Don't tell() deaths to all. Every attacked player, including those who died, gets their attack notice (R20 step 5), saying whether they died; moderators have skipped it, or left out the death, for players who died. Tell each role-blocked player that they were role-blocked, even one with no night action or who chose not to act (R9); a role-blocker learns only whether the block failed because its target can't be role-blocked (R9). Write private results in the present, about tonight ('You were role-blocked tonight'), never 'last night': they are delivered at the end of this night. Every player who used an ability gets a private result line, even when nothing else happened (e.g. 'You went on alert. 1 alert token left.'), stating any tokens they have left, except where a role note below says otherwise (e.g. code tells them, so don't tell() them a second result). Tell all Yakuza which actions each Yakuza chose but not the results, nor whether a teammate was role-blocked (R8); role-blocked Yakuza's Katana votes still count. only the attacker learns whether the Katana attack succeeded. Update token counts for any tokens spent. Before end_phase, call record_visits once with every visit that happened tonight (R6, R20 steps 1-2), as [visitor, target] pairs, a self-visit as [X, X] (an empty list if there were none). Easy to miss: the Katana holder visits the Katana target (R8) besides any visit from their own role's action; automatic visits (the Ex-Con's); a Seer's chosen pair is a visit to both players. Leave out the actions of role-blocked players, Astral Visits and actions that target no player. The submitted actions above already show any swap (R23), so record each visit to the player it landed on.

Also handle these roles' effects, using random_choice for anything random:
- A Ballot Stuffer who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the stuff_ballot op, which spends the token; code doubles their trial votes tomorrow.
- A Bounty Hunter's attack is a Strong Attack that spends its attack token: pass by=<the Bounty Hunter> on the kill op, since code credits its bounties from the killers. Code tells it which bounties it claimed or lost and handles its win or loss; don't tell() it about bounties.
- A Fixer who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the fix op, which spends the token; code counts the player's trial votes tomorrow as the opposite; nobody is told. It is a visit to the target only.
- A Juror who acted (and wasn't role-blocked) and named two different players other than themselves (target and second_target; dead players allowed): use the jury op with those two players; code tells the Juror the result. Don't tell() the Juror anything about it. It is an Astral Visit, so it visits no one.
- Ritualist who spent tokens (and wasn't role-blocked): compare the guessed role with the target's exact role (a Roleplayer is a Roleplayer). Right: deal the Attack (1 token Standard, 2 Divine). Wrong: no Attack; announce it with tell(['all'], '<name> is a Ritualist.') tonight, which is read out at the start of the next Day, even if the Ritualist dies tonight. Astral Visit.
- A Scrutineer who acted (and wasn't role-blocked): use the scrutinize op; code draws two others and tells them how many of the three voted Guilty in each of the Day's trials. Don't tell() the Scrutineer anything about it. It is an Astral Visit, so it visits no one.
- Smuggler: code has already carried out each swap below (spent the token, redirected every other action in the JSON and told the Smuggler and both swapped players), so resolve the actions as given and tell none of them about the swap. Actions it moved keep the player's own choice in `chosen_target` / `chosen_second_target`: word every private result with the player the action's user chose, never the one it landed on, and in a list of players trade the swapped pair's names (each where the other would be), so the swap stays hidden (rules R23). Give ops the player an action landed on: code words its own results this way. The Smuggler visits both swapped players (R6); it can't be role-blocked.

Use apply_changes for deaths and token/status changes, tell() for each private result, and end_phase when done. Deaths you apply are announced publicly at dawn automatically, including the kill's cause, so make the cause just the source as the rules allow it to be known (e.g. 'Katana', 'Vigilante', 'Serial Killer', 'Trap'). For each kill also set `by` to the player whose action killed them (the trap's owner for a trap) and katana=true for the Katana attack; these are recorded for analysis, never shown. Don't tell() deaths to all. Every attacked player, including those who died, gets their attack notice (R20 step 5), saying whether they died; moderators have skipped it, or left out the death, for players who died. Tell each role-blocked player that they were role-blocked, even one with no night action or who chose not to act (R9); a role-blocker learns only whether the block failed because its target can't be role-blocked (R9). Write private results in the present, about tonight ('You were role-blocked tonight'), never 'last night': they are delivered at the end of this night. Every player who used an ability gets a private result line, even when nothing else happened (e.g. 'You went on alert. 1 alert token left.'), stating any tokens they have left, except where a role note below says otherwise (e.g. code tells them, so don't tell() them a second result). Update token counts for any tokens spent. Easy to miss: the Katana holder visits the Katana target (R8) besides any visit from their own role's action; automatic visits (the Ex-Con's); a Seer's chosen pair is a visit to both players. Leave out the actions of role-blocked players, Astral Visits and actions that target no player. The submitted actions above already show any swap (R23), so record each visit to the player it landed on.

Also handle these roles' effects, using random_choice for anything random:
- A Ballot Stuffer who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the stuff_ballot op, which spends the token; code doubles their trial votes tomorrow.
- A Bounty Hunter's attack is a Strong Attack that spends its attack token: pass by=<the Bounty Hunter> on the kill op, since code credits its bounties from the killers. Code tells it which bounties it claimed or lost and handles its win or loss; don't tell() it about bounties.
- A Fixer who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the fix op, which spends the token; code counts the player's trial votes tomorrow as the opposite; nobody is told. It is a visit to the target only.

output.confusing_rules: The Katana holder-versus-attacker distinction was hard to track: a holder reads Good to alignment checks but the Sheriff reads Not Evil, and the swap rules say a Katana aimed at a swapped player lands on the partner, which several players argued about incorrectly. The Juror and Scrutineer results' timing (posted at the start of the next Day, but the trial counted before the result arrives) made it unclear when a claim could be checked. The Medic-versus-Ritualist guess timing (a right guess still lets a Medic save apply on the same night) was also not obvious.
output.missing_information: The public ledger did not show who was in each visit group or who visited whom, so most Katana-holder and visit-based claims could not be checked by anyone. The Night 2 Lookout target of Frank was never posted publicly, which the whole Village kept asking for. I also had trouble keeping the Day-by-Day nomination votes straight, since vote totals were secret but per-player votes were restated in claims that sometimes contradicted each other. A clearer per-night public log of visit counts would have helped.
output.wanted_but_couldnt: As a Ritualist I wanted to give a short, cover-friendly public statement about my own night action without revealing a live target, but the interface only let me submit or not submit a role action. I also wanted to see the living players' current token counts and remaining budget summary in one place each turn rather than piecing them together from the prompt and notepad.
output.bugs_or_oddities: Some public claims in the ledger were recorded inconsistently with what players actually posted (for example, a Juror's check pair was listed differently across days and a vote count was truncated). The ledger's 'earlier' summaries repeated claims with minor drift. The Day 5 Grace nomination total (9 Yes with 10 living voters) was consistent with the announced totals, so the confusion was in player statements, not in the moderator. The Ritualist guess that succeeded was announced only as a result to me privately, not as a public fact, which left the Village unaware of the Medic kill's cause.
output.suggestions: Publish a compact, per-night public list of visit counts (or visitor counts per target) so Katana and Bounty Hunter victims can be checked without relying on claims. Show the Day's vote roster to all players with each player's vote hidden until the total is announced, so a player's claimed vote can be cross-checked against the total. Allow a short private 'cover statement' option for Yakuza night actions, and keep the notepad and budget display in each turn prompt so the player does not have to recompute the budget from the price table.

Swap notices sent to the swapped players gave no partner name, so I could not tell which Night 4 death or protection was misrouted.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to check a specific claim against the ballot totals, for example whether a 9-of-10 count leaves one No, but I had no tool to recount it beyond manual arithmetic. I also wanted to ask the moderator for the Night 2 Lookout visitor list privately, and to query whether a Katana attack on a swapped partner would show as a visit to me; the interface gave no way to ask the moderator questions outside the fixed outputs.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: The Day 5 Grace trial and nomination counts were inconsistent with the number of living voters as stated by the program: Carol's nomination on Day 5 showed 1 Yes while the living count was 10, and the public summary text shows 'Dave's No' in a Day 5 tally after Dave had died. The Day 3 Sheriff claim text changed wording between posts (Katana holder reads Good versus Not Evil), which the summary recorded as a claim change. Several private messages were summarized only as counts, so the recipient and sender of messages could not always be matched to content. The public ledger also truncated Grace's claim with [truncated] during Day 5.
answers.suggestions: Publish a per-vote ledger after each Day (who voted Yes/No, Guilty/Innocent, with the hidden votes still secret to the public but visible to the player who cast them as a reminder). Show the number of living voters and the threshold in every vote announcement. Give swapped players the partner's seat or name when the swapped-in attack lands, or at least tell them which action was misrouted. Put a clear note in the rules that a trial-only budget and first defense message exist and how the budget carryover works, since I only learned the price table on each turn. Consider a short log of each night's visits as a reference sheet so players do not have to reconstruct visit trees from claims.

answers.confusing_rules: The Katana and swap rules were hard to apply together. A swap moves actions aimed at the swapped players, so a Katana aimed at a swapped partner lands on the partner, and a Standard save follows the same path. Several players, including Heidi and Judy, misapplied this in public. The Ballot Stuffer rule says a trial needs a majority of all votes counted, but it doesn't say whether the doubled vote is counted in that total. Alignment rules for the Katana holder also read as contradictory when stated in summary form (holder reads Good, but a Sheriff sees Not Evil). The Juror check, which compares votes only over days both players voted, was also hard to use as evidence.
answers.missing_information: I could not see the other Yakuza's night submissions until the results posted, so coordinating a single holder and target depended on trusting chat. I could not see the speaking budget or remaining words in this summary, so I could not tell whether a long message would be affordable. The public claims ledger truncated Grace's Night 4 entry, so the full claim was not visible to anyone reading the ledger. Frank's Night 2 Lookout target was announced only in a will and later in results, so it was hard to know when a claim was publicly available.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: As Ballot Stuffer I never got to use my token on a close trial because the team never reached a close vote while I was alive. I wanted a way to ask the moderator a yes or no question about whether an action would be legal before committing it at night, since the swap and Katana interactions were tangled. I also wanted to see the vote counts behind a nomination with the voter names removed, to test a claimed contradiction, but that is secret by design.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: The summary I was given after my death still contained my pre-death Yakuza night chat and my Night 3 Katana vote, which is fine, but the framing of the game state ('you have 2 ballot tokens left') read as if I were alive while the ledger listed me as dead, which was confusing. Grace's public claim contained a literal '[truncated]' marker. A Day 5 Juror claim described nominations as having 3 No votes when only 1 was living and possible, showing that claims could contain arithmetic errors the moderator did not flag. Heidi's public Day 6 story about a Night 3 swap and attack was accurate only once the swap mechanics were read carefully, and the game did not make it easy to see that the Katana landed on the partner.
answers.suggestions: Show each living player their remaining speaking budget and word count in the summary and in each prompt. Mark claims that were truncated or shortened with a clear note, and never cut a claim mid-sentence without a visible flag. For swaps, add a short plain statement of what landed where on the victim's own result, so players do not have to infer it. Clarify whether a Ballot Stuffer's doubled vote counts in the trial majority denominator. Let dead players see the public ledger state that matches their role (they already do) but state clearly when they are dead in any game-state text.

answers.confusing_rules: R23 (Swaps) was the hardest rule to apply. 'Every action aimed at one of them' does not say whether Astral Visits and checks of past Day votes are moved. I moved them. Grace's Juror check on Dave (N3) was computed on Heidi's votes, and her N4 check on Alice+Dave was computed on Alice+Niaj, while her results still named Dave. She posted '5 of 5 nominations' for Alice/Dave. Alice correctly said that was impossible, and Grace was hanged for it. That follows the letter of R23, but a check on Day votes is changed by a night swap she could not detect, and the result looks like a lie. The rules should say explicitly whether swaps affect Astral or vote-history checks (Juror, Scrutineer, Oracle, Ritualist guesses). R23 also says results 'name the player the user chose', but it does not say which name the Yakuza summary and the Katana holder's result should use when the Katana target is swapped.
answers.missing_information: I had no resolver view showing, for each action, the submitted target next to the post-swap landing target. My logs mix the two. Alice's entries list the landing target (Heidi N3, Niaj N4) with 'give Dave' in the note. Grace's entries list Heidi and Niaj while her notes say Dave. The Katana vote shows 'attacks Dave' on both N3 and N4, even though the Yakuza chat agreed on Heidi (N3) and Niaj (N4). Because of this I cannot confirm afterwards what the Yakuza actually submitted on Night 3. I also had no running ledger of each player's claimed votes against the real votes, or of Defense sources per player per night.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to see the raw submitted Katana votes separately from the resolved target, so I could check that the swap had been applied exactly once. I also wanted a per-night state table (who has what Defense, where each action landed, who was swapped) to audit before results went out, and a way to flag a suspected resolution error during the game. I flagged nothing, and I should have.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: 1) Likely resolution bug on Night 3. All eight Yakuza chat messages agreed: Katana target Heidi, Carol swaps Heidi and Dave. Alice protected Dave. Correct resolution: the Katana lands on Dave, Alice's protection lands on Heidi, so Dave (unprotected) dies. Instead nobody died. Heidi was told she was attacked with the Katana and survived, and Judy was told 'attack Dave… failed'. Night 4 had the identical decoy-plus-swap structure and correctly killed Dave, so N3 and N4 are inconsistent. Either the Katana was not moved, or it was moved twice, or the recorded votes (Dave) contradict the chat. On Day 6 Judy and Mallory publicly argued that Heidi's attack was mechanically impossible. They were right given what they had submitted, and Heidi was hanged partly over that false notice. 2) Inconsistent naming in Yakuza summaries. N3 says the vote 'sends it to attack Dave', while N4 says Judy 'attacked Niaj' (the chosen target). 3) The swap moved Grace's Astral Juror action without telling her, which produced the contradiction that got her hanged (see confusing_rules). 4) Minor issues: one claim line in the ledger was stored as '[truncated]'. The phase label 'Day 1 day' is odd. On Night 2 Erin's bounty-claimed message was delivered before her attack result. The Fixer flipped Heidi's own Innocent vote to Guilty and decided her execution, which is correct by the rules but worth noting as a high-impact silent effect.
answers.suggestions: 1) Have the program, not the moderator, resolve swaps, and print a per-action audit line: 'submitted X → landed Y'. 2) Exempt Astral Visits and Day-vote checks (Juror, Scrutineer, Auditor) from swaps, or at least say clearly that they are affected. 3) Standardize every result and summary to name the chosen target, matching R23, and log both chosen and landed targets. 4) Add a pre-dawn consistency check: every attack has a target and a Defense comparison, every notice matches a landed action, and nobody is told they were attacked unless an attack landed on them. 5) Store the raw Katana votes separately from the resolved attack. 6) Add a vote ledger for the moderator, so vote-based checks can be verified automatically. 7) Show players a reminder of the living-voter count at each vote, to cut down tally confusion like Grace's '3 No' error.

title: Post-game lessons: tips players wish they'd known, and how past tips went

task:
If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

You were also given tips from past games (in your instructions). Which of them went especially well or badly for you or others this game? List only tips that clearly mattered (or none): helped, hurt (followed it and it backfired, or it was predictable to opponents), or wrong (it is false or contradicts the rules), and why, concretely.

lessons.tip: A Katana aimed at a swapped player lands on the partner, so a swapped target can reveal the swap: check whether the 'attack survived' or 'attack landed' notices match the swap partner's visit list before accepting a survival claim.

Before accepting or rejecting a Juror, Scrutineer or Sheriff claim, check its numbers against the public vote count: with N living voters, Yes or Guilty totals fix how many No or Innocent votes there were, and a dead voter cannot cast a vote that day.

Do not let a teammate's public nomination become a Yakuza-wide vote pattern across many Days; repeated same-way votes on the same village nominees are the clearest tell that the town's analysts will use.

A confirmed Standard protection that fails against a Standard Katana attack gives a Medic-plus-Sheriff pair a strong cover; keep the protector's claim consistent across nights, because contradictory protection logs are what the town checks first.
Ask for concrete, checkable facts (a named visitor, a result, a count) rather than pressure; the town was split for days because most accusations named no visit and nobody could be checked.

tips_feedback.tip: Ballots are secret, so keep a notepad of every nomination and trial: each player's stated vote, the announced totals and your own.
tips_feedback.why: The Grace 9-Yes and 6-6 trial tallies exposed the arithmetic errors in Grace's Juror story, and the notepad tracked Judy and Mallory's matching Yes votes across Days 3 to 6.

tips_feedback.tip: Before voting Guilty, name one concrete mechanical fit: an unexplained Evil read on a Vanilla claim, a broken visit claim, or a group result where elimination leaves one name.
tips_feedback.why: Votes that cited a named visit or a checked result (Dave's Night 3 Evil on Olivia) were easier to weigh, while votes with no fact behind them, like Heidi's and Niaj's pushes, looked suspicious.

tips_feedback.tip: Never announce tonight's target, in public or by PM. A Wiretap may read every PM, and a named target tells blockers and the Katana where to go.
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza team's Katana plans were hidden, and the town could only infer the attacks from deaths and swap notices after the fact.

output.reason: Reflecting on lessons learned from this game for future play.

tips_feedback.tip: Trust checked results over bare claims.

lessons.tip: A Standard Katana attack is blanked by any Standard save, so when the Medic protects the same target every night, switch targets or combine the Katana with a Smuggler swap aimed at a decoy early rather than repeating the same attack pattern.

Spend one-shot tools (Ritualist guess, Smuggler swap, Clerk rig) only after confirming the target's role through a visible contradiction; a wrong or unnecessary guess announces you and wastes tokens with no visible gain.

Vote with the Village on Day trials where a Village-looking nominee is at risk, so your votes match the announced totals; coordinated early Yes votes on a Sheriff or Scrutineer were the public pattern that exposed our team.

Check swap arithmetic before accusing anyone: a Katana aimed at a swapped player lands on the partner, and a save aimed at one lands on the other, so a 'survived' or 'died' result can be explained by a swap rather than a visit.
Count living voters before alleging a vote tally is wrong: with n living voters, Yes plus No must equal n, and dead players cannot vote, which is how a Juror's tally error was exposed.

tips_feedback.tip: Don't defend a doomed teammate. If your team's votes can't stop the hang, vote Guilty with the town, because hidden Innocent votes show in the totals.
tips_feedback.why: Voting with the Village on the Olivia and Grace trials kept our side from being publicly marked by lonely Innocent votes, and the bulk Guilty votes did not expose us further.

tips_feedback.why: Heidi's private pushes to Bob and Niaj were visible to everyone and became the lead Village used against her, and the Heidi PM pattern helped the town converge on our side.

tips_feedback.why: Our Village-role claims (Fixer as Vanilla Villager, Ritualist as Vanilla) survived several rounds of checks, since no public result contradicted them until the Night 5 guess.

tips_feedback.tip: Every member must submit the agreed Katana holder and target every night; one missing vote can cancel the kill.
tips_feedback.why: Our unanimous submissions every night produced the kills on Dave, Ivan and Niaj without a failed-vote cancellation.

tips_feedback.why: Not applicable to our game's role list; the tip is generic and the Ritualist guess on Alice (announced publicly on death) was a Yakuza-only action the tip does not cover.

lessons.tip: A Divine guess on a Medic claim only works if the Medic's save is not already moved or blocked; spend ritual tokens only after confirming the target's role from a checked source, because a wrong guess is announced and exposes the guesser.

Before submitting a Katana holder and target, check whether any living Village player has a checked result that could expose the holder; the holder's visit is what trackers and visit-list checks see, so keep the holder's public claims consistent with it.
Count the living voters before accepting a claimed tally: with N living voters, a Yes count of Y leaves N minus Y No votes, and a dead player cannot cast a vote on a later Day.

Private messages pushing a nomination are visible to everyone as to who messaged whom; avoid sending repeated pushes to two different players about the same nominee, since that pattern is easy to spot.
Juror and Scrutineer checks name only aggregate counts; if a claimed check pair or night changes between posts, flag it immediately and ask for the night and pair before voting.

tips_feedback.why: Frank's dead Lookout claim and the Katana holder visits were used by Village players to focus suspicion on Dave and Olivia early.

Before voting on a claimed Juror or Scrutineer check, recompute the vote tally yourself from the announced total and the number of living voters; a claim that fails basic arithmetic (e.g. counting a dead player's vote) is an easy, concrete reason to vote.

Ask every claimed power role for a one-sentence visit list at the same time, and mark which claims cannot be checked before the vote; nominating people for 'no visit named' pushed the town into hanging unverified Village players, while the real Yakuza stayed alive.

Private messages are visible as sender-recipient pairs to everyone; if two players send each other or several players repeated private pushes for one nominee, that pattern is public and should be named early rather than letting it build into a bloc.

Use a Ritualist Divine guess only on a role the town has already tested, and not on a Medic claim that is only a protection claim; the guess spent two tokens and exposed the Ritualist once it was announced.

Keep the daytime voting record consistent with what you say in chat, and avoid a public Yes on nominations that name no visit when you are the only one pressing; a repeated pattern of Yes votes on Village nominees got Judy and Mallory targeted by the town and made them the lead.

Do not send private messages pushing one nominee to other players. Every PM is visible as a sender/recipient pair, and Heidi's repeated PMs to Bob and Niaj were the clearest public signal of coordination in the game.

Count living voters before accusing someone's tally: a Yes count plus No count must equal living voters, and dead players cannot vote. Several Day 5 accusations collapsed because people miscounted voters, which wasted a trial.

summary: The Yakuza won (Carol, Judy, Mallory, plus the hanged Olivia), and the Bounty Hunter Erin also won before leaving. Day 2 was spent repeating 'wait for Night 2' with no nominations. On Night 2 Erin used her Strong attack on Frank, one of her bounty targets. That killed the Lookout who had just watched Judy visit Dave, so his result was lost. The Village's one clean hit was Dave's Night 3 Evil check on Olivia, which hanged her 11-1; her teammates voted Guilty on her. The Yakuza then used Carol's Smuggler swaps against a Medic who protected Dave every night. Night 3's swap should already have killed Dave, but a moderator error saved him. Night 4's Niaj/Dave swap moved Alice's protection off Dave and killed him. On Day 5 the Village hanged Grace, a truthful Juror. Her Alice/Dave result had been distorted by that swap, she confused which day's nomination tally she meant, and Heidi miscounted against her. That hang gave Erin her second bounty. Mallory's Divine Ritualist guess on Alice (Medic) and the Katana on Ivan brought the game to 3v3. Judy secretly fixed Heidi, the Village voted Yes to put Heidi on trial, and Heidi's own Innocent vote was flipped to the decisive fourth Guilty. Bob followed the next Day. The Village had the right pattern all along: Olivia's 4-Yes nomination of Dave and the 4 Guilty votes on Ivan were exactly the four Yakuza. Ivan's Night 3 scrutiny (2 of Carol, Erin and Olivia Guilty on Ivan) pinned Carol, but he never posted that half. Heidi kept her Night 3 swap-and-attack notice secret until Day 6.

lessons.tip: When the Village is at or near parity, never vote Yes to put a player on trial without a real case. Assume a Fixer or Ballot Stuffer can turn any trial. Count the likely evil bloc and keep nominations from passing unless the Village alone can control the trial.
lessons.evidence: At 3v3 on Day 6, Bob and Niaj voted Yes on Mallory's nomination of Heidi (5 Yes). Judy had fixed Heidi that night, so Heidi's own Innocent vote counted as Guilty. The trial passed 4-2 when it should have been 3-3, and the Village lost a member and then the game.

lessons.tip: Build a vote table early and look for a fixed bloc. A failed nomination with N Yes votes, and the matching Guilty count in a trial, often equals the evil team exactly. Post every part of a vote-count result, because a partial count can name the last member of the bloc.
lessons.evidence: Olivia's nomination of Dave got exactly 4 Yes (Olivia, Carol, Judy, Mallory), and Ivan's trial got exactly those 4 Guilty. Ivan's Night 3 scrutiny showed 2 of Carol, Erin and Olivia Guilty in his trial. Erin had claimed Innocent, so that meant Carol and Olivia, completing the bloc. Ivan only posted the Grace-trial count. Nobody named the unclaimed fourth Yes until Day 6, when it was too late.

lessons.tip: Before hanging an investigator whose result looks impossible, check whether a public swap notice from that night could have redirected it. Also make sure everyone is talking about the same Day's tally. A swap explains a strange result the way a role-block explains a missing one.
lessons.evidence: Grace's Night 4 Juror check on Alice and Dave actually landed on Alice and Niaj, because Niaj and Dave were swapped. Niaj had posted his swap notice that same Day. The Village still called Grace's 5-of-5 a lie. Heidi read Grace's '9 Yes, 3 No' (Grace's own Day 3 nomination) as the Day 5 tally, and a truthful Juror was hanged 8-2.

lessons.tip: Post private night notices (swapped, attacked and survived, role-blocked) on the next Day. They reveal enemy tools such as a Smuggler and confirm protectors. Kept until you are on trial, they look made up.
lessons.evidence: Heidi was told on Night 3 that she was swapped and survived a Katana attack. That would have shown a Smuggler and a moved Medic save, and warned Alice before Night 4. She first mentioned it on her Day 6 trial, and Judy, Mallory and Carol attacked it as a mechanics lie.

lessons.tip: Don't protect the same claimed power role every night once a Smuggler or swap is possible. Vary your target, or spend a token on Strong or self-protection. A fixed pattern lets the Smuggler swap your save away.
lessons.evidence: Alice protected Dave on Nights 2, 3 and 4. Carol's Night 4 swap of Niaj and Dave sent Alice's save to Niaj and the Katana to Dave, who died. Alice died with both medic tokens unused, to a Divine Ritualist guess.

lessons.tip: Use your strong tools together on the confirmed threats. Use a Smuggler decoy swap against a predictable protector, and a Divine Ritualist guess only on a role you are sure of, such as a claimed Medic whose saves fit. Save a Fixer for the parity trial, on a Villager likely to vote Innocent.
lessons.evidence: Carol aimed the Katana at a decoy and swapped the decoy with Dave, which killed Dave on Night 4. Mallory's Divine guess of Alice as Medic was right on Night 5. Judy's fix on Heidi turned Heidi's Innocent into the decisive Guilty on Day 6.

lessons.tip: Claim Vanilla, use your single Strong attack early on a target the town won't miss, and push your other targets toward trial with the town's own reasoning, such as 'no results'. Your Guilty vote must count on the hang.
lessons.evidence: Erin killed Frank (a bounty target) on Night 2 under a Vanilla claim. She nominated Grace on Day 3 for having no results, kept pressing her, and voted Guilty when Grace was hanged on Day 5, winning before anyone suspected her.

lessons.tip: On a Day with no information, don't spend the whole Day repeating 'wait for results'. Use it to put votes on record or test claims, or let it end quickly. Endless filler gives evil free cover and pushes real work onto Days when power roles are already dead.
lessons.evidence: Day 2 had about 70 near-identical 'no nomination until Night 2' messages and no votes. The only useful moment was Heidi questioning Grace's Juror wording.

tips_feedback.tip: Don't defend a doomed teammate. If your team's votes can't stop the hang, vote Guilty with the town, because hidden Innocent votes show in the totals.
tips_feedback.why: Carol, Judy and Mallory voted Guilty on Olivia (11-1), which hid the bloc. Only their No votes on her nomination were later noticed, and too late.

tips_feedback.tip: A swap moves only actions aimed at the two swapped players. Aim the Katana at a decoy and swap the decoy with the protected real target.
tips_feedback.why: Carol did exactly this on Nights 3 and 4. Night 4 killed the confirmed Sheriff through Alice's protection.

tips_feedback.tip: Use free Standard protection on likely Katana targets, vary your pattern, and never announce targets. Spend a token on self-protection within a night or two of claiming.
tips_feedback.why: Alice ignored the 'vary' and 'self-protect' parts, protecting Dave three nights in a row. The Smuggler exploited the pattern, and she died with 2 tokens unspent. The tip was right; not following it cost the Village.

tips_feedback.tip: Totals can be manipulated. A trial total above the voter count means a Ballot Stuffer, and a Fixer silently flips one player's trial votes. Yes/No nomination counts can't be altered, so they are the cleanest liar check.
tips_feedback.why: Heidi and Bob used the unalterable 4-Yes count on Dave's nomination to find Carol as the unclaimed Yes, which was correct. Nobody acted on the Fixer warning, and a fix decided Heidi's trial.

tips_feedback.tip: Once someone is shown Yakuza mechanically, look at who defended them or pushed to delay their hang.
tips_feedback.why: After Olivia's Evil check, Bob, Heidi and Niaj correctly pointed at Judy and Mallory voting with Olivia on Dave and Ivan. It came on Day 6, too late to win.

tips_feedback.tip: Post your role, target and exact result in your first speech after getting it.
tips_feedback.why: Dave posted his Olivia Evil result first thing on Day 4, and she was hanged. Ivan posted only part of his scrutiny; the unposted Ivan-trial count would have pinned Carol.

tips_feedback.tip: Tokens die with you. Spend one-shot tokens on the first Day or night they can change a vote or remove a threat.
tips_feedback.why: Judy's fix and Mallory's Divine guess were spent at decisive moments and won the game. Olivia and Alice both died holding unused tokens.

issues.description: Night 3: the swap was applied twice. The Yakuza aimed the Katana at Heidi, and Carol swapped Heidi with Dave. The code line already showed the post-swap target ('Judy holds it and attacks Dave'). The moderator then treated Dave as the chosen target and moved the attack back onto Heidi. Alice's Standard protection, aimed at Dave, correctly landed on Heidi, so Dave had Defense None and should have died to the Katana. No death was applied. Heidi was falsely told she survived a Katana attack, and Dave got no attack notice. Judy was told her attack on Dave failed, when she should have been told her attack on Heidi succeeded. The Yakuza summary also named Dave as the target instead of the chosen target, Heidi. The visit was also recorded as Judy->Heidi instead of Judy->Dave.

The automated night check flagged several high-severity Night 3 errors at the start of Day 4, including a missed death, but nothing was corrected and the game went on with the wrong state. Dave, who should have died, survived, nominated Olivia and got her hanged. Heidi later used the false 'attacked and survived' notice in her trial defense. The game outcome was materially changed by an error the harness had detected.

The Katana line given to the moderator on swap nights ('Katana: Judy holds it and attacks Dave') shows the already-swapped target without saying the swap has been applied. On Night 3 this likely caused the moderator to apply the swap a second time. Night 4 was resolved correctly, so the input format is ambiguous. It should state both the chosen target and the post-swap landing target.

Day 5: Grace's Juror result was correct (the Night 4 swap redirected her Dave pick onto Niaj, so Alice+Niaj matched 5 of 5 nominations). Players instead argued it was false, using Day 5 votes the check doesn't cover. Several also confused which nomination had 9 Yes of 10 voters (Heidi spoke of 'the Carol nomination'). Grace herself miscounted by including dead Dave's No. Nobody considered that Grace's Juror pick on Dave could have been redirected by the Night 4 swap that Alice and Niaj had just deduced. This led to a Village Juror being hanged.

The ledger truncated Grace's Day 5 claim ('[truncated]'), and players said in feedback that this made it harder to rebuild the per-vote record. Heidi and Bob also had empty answers cut off at max_tokens and needed effort-fallback retries.

When Erin (Bounty Hunter) won and left the game, her last will was published. The rules say wills are shared 'when a player dies', and leaving 'works exactly like dying' except it isn't a death. Whether a leaving player's will is revealed is not stated explicitly.
